html:
The Tlatelolco massacre took place on 2 October 1968 in the Plaza of the Three Cultures in Mexico City. Soldiers and police fired on a meeting of students and others, killing many; estimates range from about thirty to over three hundred.

That summer, students had marched against police brutality and the one-party rule of the PRI, the party that had governed since the revolution. President Gustavo Díaz Ordaz, with the Olympic Games about to open in Mexico, wanted order. On the evening of 2 October, as the meeting ended, flares were fired and troops surrounded the square and opened fire.

The government blamed the students and hid the death toll for decades. The Olympics opened ten days later. The massacre became a lasting wound. The PRI lost the presidency only in 2000, after the Zapatista uprising and the crises of the 1990s. Each 2 October, people march in Mexico City in memory.
